questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing. This helps you see farther ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: The group will exit at the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: When the lead rider raises their left arm and points with one finger, it signals all riders to form a single-file line.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than those wearing helmets.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobbling?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road surface.
questions.explanation: Wobbling is usually caused by wrong tire pressure, improper weight distribution, or wrong accessories. Do not try to speed up to stop a wobble.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Keep you away from wind blasts from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen. It should protect you from wind blasts and surface hazards, not place you in blind spots. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and provide an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When a group of motorcyclists enters a highway or curve, they should:

options.text: Ride on the far right of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is fine on straight roads.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at about a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or seams at least at a 45-degree angle. Make a quick, sharp turn. Crossing slowly or at a small angle can catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: When it is raining, where is the safest place to ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Rain makes roads very slippery, especially at first. Oil from cars has not yet washed away. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is often the best choice.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to wobble or shake?

options.text: Brakes that do not work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Wobbling is usually caused by wrong tire pressure, improper weight distribution, or unsuitable accessories.

questions.question: If you must swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left handlegrip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handlegrip, then the left.

questions.question: As the motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should lessen the amount of pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward during braking, the front wheel has more traction. This means you can press the front brake harder.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the direction opposite of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left handlegrip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handlegrip, then the left.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move around while you are riding. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as close to you as possible without getting in your way and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you come to a full stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever so the tire can grip again. Then reapply the brake.

questions.question: To best control a motorcycle, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with their arms fully extended.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are used for rules and regulations like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the tail end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves right behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the brake until the rear tire regains traction, then re-apply the brake.
Release the brake and only engage the front brake.
Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a stop.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: At a minimum, how often should a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid be checked?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluid and coolant at least once a week as part of regular motorcycle maintenance before riding.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups should ride in single-file when going through curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. Staggered formations are used at other times.

questions.question: The best way to brake in a straight line is to:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Does not mean that they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver sees you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles and still fail to notice them.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible before hitting the object. Try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The near side of the lane is safer.
You are more likely to feel wind from the passing vehicle on the far side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane closer to the passing vehicle. Moving to the far side may encourage the driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: How does the stopping distance for motorcycles compare to cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, on slippery pavement, motorcycles have much more trouble stopping quickly.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to protect from wind, cold, and rain.
Ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect from wind, cold, and rain.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Limit riding to no more than six hours per day. Take rest breaks at least every two hours. Avoid caffeine and artificial stimulants, as they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have had less than six months of experience on the motorcycle they were riding.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and appear to move more slowly than they really do. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their actual location and speed.
